adjacent_skills.jd_skill: AI tools / high velocity engineering workflows

key_responsibilities: Build and deploy ML models for core Snapchat products
Apply established ML techniques to well-defined problems
Data analysis, model training, evaluation, production deployment
Collaborate cross-functionally to launch ML-driven features
Use AI tools and high velocity workflows to ship scalable services

strengths: Deep ML training/evaluation experience with measured before/after gains — DONUT visual-document-understanding transformer fine-tuning (55%->93% validation accuracy), U-Net medical segmentation (Dice/IoU), YOLOv8 detection (83% mAP@50)
Genuine content-understanding depth via DONUT/VisionEncoderDecoder (structured field extraction from documents) — real backing for the "content understanding" ask, just never string-matched
Cross-functional collaboration and delivery under pressure — took over as team lead mid-project on the Teesside BraTS segmentation project, restructured a 7-person team, delivered in a 6-week window
Comfortable applying established ML techniques to well-defined problems across many short projects (transfer learning, fine-tuning, quantization)
real_gaps: No ranking system experience of any kind (learning-to-rank, relevance scoring, feed ranking)
No recommendation system experience (collaborative filtering, embeddings-based retrieval, candidate generation)
No generative image modeling experience (GANs, diffusion, text-to-image) — profile work is discriminative/perception (detection, segmentation, depth), not generative

No large-scale backend/service ML deployment — "production deployment" in the profile means single-device edge inference (Jetson + TensorRT), not the scalable, high-velocity backend services Snap describes
No experience with a social-media-scale product surface or its data characteristics (engagement signals, feed dynamics, content moderation)
overstated_by_keywords: production deployment — counted Adjacent by the keyword pass, but the actual depth is edge/embedded single-device deployment, a meaningfully different discipline from scalable backend ML services
understated_by_keywords: DONUT/VisionEncoderDecoder document understanding work is stronger real backing for "content understanding" than the keyword pass gave credit for
Team-lead delivery under a hard deadline (Teesside) is concrete evidence for the "collaborate cross-functionally to launch features" responsibility, not just a generic soft-skill checkbox
screening_gaps: Zero backing for ranking/recommendations/search — the three responsibilities most central to what Snap actually builds (feed ranking, content recs, search) with no adjacent evidence at all
No generative image modeling experience for the explicit "image generation" ask

Production deployment experience is edge/single-device, not the scalable backend services the JD centers on — a recruiter reading "Snapchat-scale ML service" against an edge-AI resume will read this as a domain mismatch, not a stretch
llm_analysis.reasoning: The ML fundamentals are real — training, evaluation, and applying established techniques are well evidenced across multiple projects with measured results. But the role is defined by ranking, recommendations, search, and content understanding at social-app scale, and the profile has zero backing for the first three and only edge-scale, not service-scale, deployment experience. This reads as a strong ML generalist applying into a domain (large-scale recommender/ranking systems) it has never touched.
